title_en: Supreme People's Court Releases Typical Cases of Crimes Endangering Food and Drug Safety
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Release of Typical Criminal Cases of Endangering Food and Drug Safety

Case 1

Defendant Zheng Liqiao and Luo Liuqing — Production and Sale of Toxic and Harmful Food

——Adding Formaldehyde to Cow Blood Curd for Preservation Resulted in Sentencing

(1) Brief Facts

Defendant Zheng Liqiao, male, born April 4, 1981, Han ethnicity, farmer.

Defendant Luo Liuqing, male, born May 28, 1972, Han ethnicity, farmer.

In September 2010, without applying for a production and operation license, Defendant Zheng Liqiao rented a residential house in Hangu Town, Jiulongpo District, Chongqing, and began processing and producing cow blood curd as food, hiring Defendant Luo Liuqing to jointly produce it. During the processing of the cow blood curd, both defendants, knowing that formaldehyde was harmful to human health, added it for preservation. By the time the case was discovered on March 17, 2011, Zheng Liqiao and Luo Liuqing had cumulatively processed and produced over 500,000 jin of cow blood curd containing formaldehyde, which was sold to various local farmers' markets, with sales amounting to RMB 125,000.

(2) Judgment

The Jiulongpo District People's Court of Chongqing held in its judgment that Defendants Zheng Liqiao and Luo Liuqing, by adulterating the cow blood curd they produced and sold with the toxic and harmful non-food raw material formaldehyde, had constituted the crime of producing and selling toxic and harmful food. They were lawfully sentenced as follows: Defendant Zheng Liqiao was sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of five years and fined RMB 250,000; Defendant Luo Liuqing was sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of four years and fined RMB 180,000; the seized tools used for the crime were confiscated; and the illegal gains of RMB 30,000 were ordered to be recovered. After the judgment was pronounced, the defendants did not appeal, and the procuratorial authority did not protest. This judgment became legally effective on June 8, 2011.

Case 2

Defendants Hu Changbin, Ke Mingzhi, Chen Hongyong, et al. — Production and Sale of Counterfeit and Substandard Products, Production and Sale of Food Not Conforming to Hygiene Standards

——Processing and Selling Meat from Diseased and Dead Pigs Constituted Concurrence of Crimes, the Heavier Charge Applied

(1) Brief Facts

Defendant Hu Changbin, male, born May 5, 1968, Han ethnicity, farmer.

Defendant Ke Mingzhi, male, born June 3, 1970, Han ethnicity, farmer.

Defendant Chen Hongyong, male, born July 30, 1968, Han ethnicity, self-employed individual.

Defendant Huang Shenghua, male, born October 9, 1964, Han ethnicity, farmer.

Defendant Yang Jinhe, male, born December 21, 1946, Han ethnicity, farmer.

Defendant Chen Guoyi, male, born October 27, 1957, Han ethnicity, farmer.

In October 2010, Defendant Hu Changbin leased an abandoned pig farm located in Nanfeng Village, Honglu Street, Fuqing City, Fujian Province, from Lin Dinghua (separately prosecuted), engaging in the processing, production, and sale of meat from diseased and dead pigs. In January 2011, Hu Changbin began cooperating with Defendant Ke Mingzhi in processing, producing, and selling such meat. By March 2011, Hu Changbin and Ke Mingzhi had slaughtered and processed over 100 tons of meat from diseased and dead pigs (collected or purchased) into ribs, meat, pigskin, sausages, etc., which were sold as food to areas in Shandong, Zhejiang, and Fujian Provinces, with sales amounting to over RMB 540,000. Among these, they purchased approximately 2.5 tons of diseased and dead pigs from Defendant Huang Shenghua, approximately 2.5 tons from Defendant Yang Jinhe, and approximately 0.5 tons from Defendant Chen Guoyi. During this period, Defendant Chen Hongyong twice purchased approximately 11 tons of meat from diseased and dead pigs from Hu Changbin and Ke Mingzhi, paying a total of RMB 30,000. On March 14, 2011, law enforcement authorities conducted an inspection of the processing and sales site of Hu Changbin and Ke Mingzhi, seizing 5.93 tons of meat from diseased and dead pigs on the spot. Inspection confirmed that the seized pork tested positive for porcine circovirus type 2.

On March 29, 2011, Hu Changbin and Ke Mingzhi again went to Shangjing Town, Fuqing City, to purchase two large bags of meat from diseased and dead pigs. They were intercepted by public security authorities while transporting the meat back to the processing site. Inspection confirmed that the samples tested positive for highly pathogenic porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome virus (PRRSV) and porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome virus.

(2) Judgment

The Fuqing City People's Court judgment and the Fuzhou Intermediate People's Court ruling held that Defendants Hu Changbin and Ke Mingzhi, knowing that meat from diseased and dead pigs was unfit for human consumption and that its consumption could cause serious food poisoning accidents or other serious foodborne diseases, nevertheless jointly processed, produced, and sold such meat, thereby constituting the crime of producing and selling food not conforming to hygiene standards. At the same time, Hu Changbin and Ke Mingzhi processed and produced meat from diseased and dead pigs and sold it as qualified pork, with sales amounting to over RMB 540,000, which also constituted the crime of producing and selling counterfeit and substandard products. Pursuant to law, they should be convicted and punished for the more serious crime, namely, producing and selling counterfeit and substandard products. Defendants Chen Hongyong, Huang Shenghua, Yang Jinhe, and Chen Guoyi, knowing the meat was from diseased and dead pigs, still sold it, thereby constituting the crime of producing and selling food not conforming to hygiene standards. Defendant Chen Guoyi voluntarily surrendered after committing the crime and truthfully confessed his criminal facts, constituting voluntary surrender, and was lawfully given a lighter punishment. Defendants Chen Hongyong, Huang Shenghua, and Yang Jinhe truthfully confessed their criminal facts after being brought to justice and were lawfully given lighter punishments. The court lawfully adjudicated as follows: Defendant Hu Changbin was convicted of producing and selling counterfeit and substandard products, sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of 11 years and six months, deprivation of political rights for one year, and fined RMB 1,000,000; Defendant Ke Mingzhi was convicted of producing and selling counterfeit and substandard products, sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of 11 years, deprivation of political rights for one year, and fined RMB 1,000,000; Defendant Chen Hongyong was convicted of producing and selling food not conforming to hygiene standards, sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of two years and nine months, and fined RMB 50,000; Defendant Huang Shenghua was convicted of producing and selling food not conforming to hygiene standards, sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of two years and six months, and fined RMB 10,000; Defendant Yang Jinhe was convicted of producing and selling food not conforming to hygiene standards, sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of two years and three months, and fined RMB 10,000; Defendant Chen Guoyi was convicted of producing and selling food not conforming to hygiene standards, sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of one year and three months, and fined RMB 3,000; the tools used for the crime were confiscated, and the illegal gains of each defendant were ordered to be further recovered.

The rulings for all defendants in this case became legally effective on April 9, 2012.

Case 3

Defendant Entity Longhai Haixin Feed Premix Co., Ltd. and Defendants Cai Shuntian, Huang Shukuan, et al. — Illegal Business Operation Case

——A Feed Company Committed an Upstream Crime Jeopardizing Food Safety and Was Sentenced

(1) Brief Facts

Defendant Entity: Longhai Haixin Feed Premix Co., Ltd.

Defendant Cai Shuntian, male, born October 7, 1966, Han ethnicity, General Manager of Longhai Haixin Feed Premix Co., Ltd.

Defendant Huang Shukuan, female, born January 5, 1964, Han ethnicity, Financial Accountant of Longhai Haixin Feed Premix Co., Ltd.

Defendant Cai Fuming, male, born February 16, 1960, Han ethnicity, Salesperson of Longhai Haixin Feed Premix Co., Ltd.

Defendant Gan Fenghua, female, born August 4, 1975, Han ethnicity, Cashier of Longhai Haixin Feed Premix Co., Ltd.

Defendant Guo Yaoqing, female, born March 22, 1978, Han ethnicity, Shipping Clerk of Longhai Haixin Feed Premix Co., Ltd.

In 2008, the Nutrition Research and Development Department of the defendant entity Longhai Haixin Feed Premix Co., Ltd. (hereinafter “Haixin Feed Company”) developed a feed additive, referred to as the core material. Haixin Feed Company added this core material to its Lvbao 18 large pig premix feed for sale. In October 2010, after feed containing the core material was found to contain prohibited ingredients, Haixin Feed Company decided to stop producing the core material. Subsequently, customers repeatedly requested Defendant Cai Shuntian, the General Manager of Haixin Feed Company, to purchase feed with feeding effects similar to the Lvbao 18 premix. In early January 2011, Cai Shuntian convened a meeting with Defendants Huang Shukuan and Gan Fenghua regarding whether to resume production of the core material. After discussion, the three defendants, knowing that the core material contained toxic, harmful, and prohibited ingredients, nevertheless decided to have the Nutrition Research and Development Department of Haixin Feed Company resume production of the core material, setting the price at RMB 450 per kilogram. Cai Shuntian was responsible for contacting customers, Huang Shukuan managed the bank account designated for receiving payments, and Gan Fenghua was responsible for withdrawing and transferring funds. After the meeting, Cai Shuntian hired Defendants Cai Fuming and Guo Yaoqing to be responsible for sales and transshipment of the core material, informing them that the core material was a feed additive not approved by the state for production and could not be sold openly, implying that it contained substances prohibited by the state. From January to March 2011, using chemical raw materials such as nitric acid, methanol, and ethyl acetate, Haixin Feed Company organized workers in the Nutrition Research and Development Department to produce core material raw powder through chemical synthesis, which was then mixed with zeolite powder for dilution and packaged in unmarked white woven bags. During this period, Haixin Feed Company sold a total of 3,000 kilograms of core material, with sales amounting to RMB 1,630,000 and illegal profits of RMB 200,000. Appraisal confirmed that the core material sold by Haixin Feed Company contained phenylethanolamine A (clenbuterol amine), a substance explicitly prohibited by the state from being added to feed and drinking water for animals. After the case was discovered, Defendants Gan Fenghua and Guo Yaoqing voluntarily surrendered to public security authorities and truthfully confessed their involvement in the crime of illegal business operation.

(2) Judgment

The Yunxi District People's Court of Yueyang City held in its judgment that the defendant entity Longhai Haixin Feed Premix Co., Ltd., by violating state regulations and producing and selling substances explicitly prohibited by the state from being added to feed, with sales amounting to RMB 1,630,000, disrupted market order, constituted a particularly serious circumstance, and thereby committed the crime of illegal business operation. Defendant Cai Shuntian, as the directly responsible supervisor of Haixin Feed Premix Co., Ltd., and Defendants Huang Shukuan, Cai Fuming, Gan Fenghua, and Guo Yaoqing, as other persons directly responsible, should be held criminally liable according to law. Among them, Cai Shuntian played a primary decision-making role in the entity's crime; Huang Shukuan, Cai Fuming, and Gan Fenghua played major roles in the crime and were all principals; Guo Yaoqing played a secondary role and was an accessory, and should be given a lighter or mitigated punishment according to law; Gan Fenghua and Guo Yaoqing constituted voluntary surrender and could be given a lighter or mitigated punishment according to law. The court lawfully adjudicated as follows: the defendant entity Longhai Haixin Feed Premix Co., Ltd. was convicted of illegal business operation and fined RMB 1,000,000; Defendant Cai Shuntian was sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of 12 years, deprivation of political rights for two years, and fined RMB 1,000,000; Defendant Huang Shukuan was sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of six years and fined RMB 700,000; Defendant Cai Fuming was sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of five years and fined RMB 600,000; Defendant Gan Fenghua was sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of four years and fined RMB 500,000; Defendant Guo Yaoqing was sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of two years and fined RMB 400,000; the illegal gains of the defendant entity Longhai Haixin Feed Premix Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 1,630,000 were ordered to be recovered and turned over to the State Treasury. After the judgment was pronounced, the defendant entity and each defendant did not appeal, and the procuratorial authority did not protest. This judgment became legally effective on February 15, 2012.

Case 4

Defendant Ma Xiaorong — Production and Sale of Toxic and Harmful Food

——Adding Poppy Seed Powder to Noodle Soup Base Resulted in Sentencing

(1) Brief Facts

Defendant Ma Xiaorong, male, born August 28, 1982, Hui ethnicity, self-employed individual.

In June 2011, Defendant Ma Xiaorong purchased poppy seeds ground into powder and mixed them into the seasoning for his noodle soup. Starting June 8, Ma Xiaorong added the seasoning containing poppy seed powder to the noodle soup at his “Jinjin Youwei Beef Noodle Restaurant” located in Jinfeng District, Yinchuan City, to produce beef noodles for sale, priced at RMB 4 to 4.5 per bowl. By June 27, the beef noodle restaurant was sealed by the Jinfeng District Health and Food and Drug Administration of Yinchuan City after the noodle soup was found to contain narcotine, papaverine, thebaine, codeine, and morphine.

(2) Judgment

The Jinfeng District People's Court of Yinchuan City held in its judgment that Defendant Ma Xiaorong, knowing that poppy seeds were toxic and harmful substances prohibited from being added to food, nevertheless added poppy seed powder to his food for sale for profit, thereby constituting the crime of producing and selling toxic and harmful food. Ma Xiaorong demonstrated a good attitude of admitting guilt, which could be considered as a discretionary circumstance for a lighter punishment. The court lawfully sentenced Defendant Ma Xiaorong to fixed-term imprisonment of nine months and fined him RMB 6,000; the unused noodle soup seasoning was confiscated. After the judgment was pronounced, the defendant did not appeal, and the procuratorial authority did not protest. This judgment became legally effective on February 2, 2012.

Case 5

Defendant Yang Tao — Sale of Toxic and Harmful Food

——Selling Health Food Illegally Adulterated with Drugs Resulted in Sentencing

(1) Brief Facts

Defendant Yang Tao, female, born January 2, 1979, Han ethnicity, Legal Representative of Shanghai Shengyu Biotechnology Co., Ltd.

From late 2007 to early 2008, Defendant Yang Tao began selling weight-loss health foods, including “Tiantianxue Brand Qingjian Runchang Capsules,” purchased from Guangzhou and other places, through physical stores and online shops. On March 9, 2011, staff from the Zhabei District Food and Drug Administration of Shanghai seized eight categories of weight-loss health foods, including “Likeke Tiantianxue Qingjian Runchang Capsules,” “Tiantianxue Brand Qingjian Runchang Capsules (Flash Super Slim),” and “Qiaomei Brand Slimming Capsules,” totaling 51 cases and 4,089 boxes, from a warehouse rented by Yang Tao. The staff orally informed Yang Tao that these health foods might contain toxic or harmful ingredients and prohibited their sale during the seizure period. Thereafter, Yang Tao continued to sell over 100 boxes of the aforementioned weight-loss health foods through her online shop until the case was uncovered. Tests confirmed that all these weight-loss health foods contained “sibutramine,” a substance explicitly prohibited by the state from being produced, sold, or used, and the illegally added drug component “phenolphthalein.” All eight categories of weight-loss health foods were toxic and harmful foods. On April 25, 2011, Yang Tao voluntarily surrendered to public security authorities and truthfully confessed her criminal facts.

(2) Judgment

The Zhabei District People's Court of Shanghai held in its judgment that Defendant Yang Tao, having been informed by law enforcement personnel that the weight-loss health foods she sold might contain toxic or harmful ingredients and were prohibited from sale, still proceeded to sell them. Her conduct constituted the sale of food knowingly adulterated with toxic and harmful non-food raw materials, thereby constituting the crime of selling toxic and harmful food. Yang Tao had the circumstance of voluntary surrender and could be given a lighter punishment according to law. The court convicted Yang Tao of the crime of selling toxic and harmful food, sentenced her to fixed-term imprisonment of three years, and fined her RMB 10,000; the illegal gains and the seized toxic and harmful foods were confiscated. After the judgment was pronounced, the defendant did not appeal, and the procuratorial authority did not protest. This judgment became legally effective on September 26, 2011.

Case 6

Defendant Zhang Jinyong — Production and Sale of Food Not Conforming to Hygiene Standards

——Abusing Food Additives Causing Poisoning Resulted in Sentencing

(1) Brief Facts

Defendant Zhang Jinyong, male, born August 26, 1975, Han ethnicity, unlicensed individual vendor.

Starting from March 2010, without obtaining industrial and commercial registration or food hygiene permits, Defendant Zhang Jinyong processed and produced raw chicken skewers at his temporary residence in Jinhui Town, Fengxian District, Shanghai, and sold them for profit. During the processing and production, Zhang Jinyong, knowing that the food additive sodium nitrite must be used within limited amounts (maximum limit value: 0.15 g/kg), nevertheless excessively added it in the production of raw chicken skewers. He subsequently sold the skewers multiple times to an individual vendor, Xu Haiping (separately prosecuted). On March 8, 2011, Xu Haiping fried and sold raw chicken skewers purchased from Zhang Jinyong outside the West Street farmers' market in Jinhui Town, Fengxian District. Four children developed symptoms of nitrite (the main component being sodium nitrite) poisoning after consuming the skewers and were hospitalized. Subsequent testing confirmed that the raw chicken skewers seized from Zhang Jinyong and Xu Haiping contained nitrite levels that severely exceeded the national standard limits.

(2) Judgment

The Fengxian District People's Court of Shanghai judgment and the Shanghai No. 1 Intermediate People's Court ruling held that Defendant Zhang Jinyong, without industrial and commercial registration and hygiene permits, produced and sold food without a license, and, knowing that the food additive sodium nitrite must be used within standard limits, excessively used it in the production of food and sold it, causing several children to suffer poisoning after consumption, thereby causing serious harm to human health. His conduct occurred before the implementation of the Criminal Law Amendment (VIII). In accordance with the principle of applying the old law and the lighter punishment, the provisions of Article 143 of the 1997 Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China were applicable, meaning that Defendant Zhang Jinyong's conduct constituted the crime of producing and selling food not conforming to hygiene standards. Zhang Jinyong truthfully confessed his criminal facts after being apprehended and could be given a lighter punishment according to law. Considering the criminal facts, circumstances, harmful consequences, and attitude of admitting guilt of Defendant Zhang Jinyong, he was sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of four years and fined RMB 1,000; the seized raw chicken skewers and sodium nitrite were confiscated.

The ruling for the defendant in this case became legally effective on November 16, 2011.

Case 7

Defendant Rao Xiuxiang — Production and Sale of Counterfeit Medicines

——Selling Medicine Packaging to Others for Producing Counterfeit Medicines Also Constituted a Crime

(1) Brief Facts

Defendant Rao Xiuxiang, female, born April 27, 1968, Han ethnicity, cleaner at Zhejiang Provincial Tongde Hospital.

From May to early November 2011, Defendant Rao Xiuxiang, taking advantage of her convenience as a cleaner at Zhejiang Provincial Tongde Hospital, and knowing that others were producing and selling counterfeit medicines, collected intact and clean Taineng medicine boxes from the trash bins in the hospital's ward pharmacy and sold them to Wang Yongfang (separately prosecuted), earning a total of over RMB 500 in illegal profits.

(2) Judgment

The Xihu District People's Court of Hangzhou City held in its judgment that Defendant Rao Xiuxiang should have known that others were purchasing medicine packaging for the purpose of manufacturing and selling counterfeit medicines. To seek illegal gains, she violated hospital regulations strictly prohibiting the private sale of medical waste, collected medicine packaging, and sold it, thereby providing assistance to those producing and selling counterfeit medicines. Her conduct constituted the crime of producing and selling counterfeit medicines. The court lawfully sentenced Defendant Rao Xiuxiang to fixed-term imprisonment of ten months and fined her RMB 1,000; the illegal gains of RMB 500 were ordered to be recovered and turned over to the State Treasury. After the judgment was pronounced, the defendant did not appeal, and the procuratorial authority did not protest. This judgment became legally effective on April 12, 2012.

Case 8

Defendants Wang Hui, Xu Hongde, Yu Hongquan, et al. — Production and Sale of Counterfeit and Substandard Products Case

——Manufacturing and Selling Counterfeit Imported Anti-Tumor Drugs Sentenced Under a Heavier Charge

(1) Brief Facts

Defendant Wang Hui, male, born January 28, 1963, Han ethnicity, Legal Representative of Shaanxi Weida Pharmaceutical E-commerce Co., Ltd.

Defendant Xu Hongde, male, born April 24, 1988, Han ethnicity, farmer.

Defendant Yu Hongquan, male, born November 6, 1977, Han ethnicity, farmer.

Defendant Zhang Xiaofeng, male, born June 28, 1962, Han ethnicity, employee of Shaanxi Weida Pharmaceutical E-commerce Co., Ltd.

In May 2004, the defendant Wang Hui and his wife Ren Jing registered and established Shaanxi New Century Pharmaceutical Technology Co., Ltd., with Wang Hui serving as the legal representative and general manager. The company's business scope mainly included technology development and consulting for pharmaceutical products, as well as the sale of medical devices. In September 2007, the company name was changed to Shaanxi Weida Pharmaceutical E-commerce Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Weida Company"), and its business scope was expanded to include internet pharmaceutical information services. Since its establishment, the company had not obtained a national drug business license or qualification certification for Good Manufacturing Practice for Drugs. In April 2009, Wang Hui, through the internet, contacted the defendant Xu Hongde, who was based in Beijing and specialized in dealing in counterfeit imported brand anti-tumor drugs. Knowing that Xu Hongde did not have the qualifications to engage in drug business, could not provide inspection reports for imported drugs or registration certificates for imported drugs, and that the source of the imported anti-tumor drugs he provided was unclear, Wang Hui purchased imported anti-tumor drugs from Xu Hongde. Xu Hongde sold to Wang Hui anti-tumor drugs of imported brands that were self-made or of unclear origin. From April 17, 2009, to January 26, 2011, Wang Hui paid a total of RMB 1,907,660 to Xu Hongde via bank transfer for the drugs. In September 2009, Wang Hui, through information posted on the internet by the defendant Yu Hongquan, contacted him and purchased from Yu Hongquan imported brand anti-tumor drugs that lacked inspection reports for imported drugs and registration certificates for imported drugs. From September 14, 2009, to January 20, 2010, Wang Hui paid a total of RMB 480,440 to Yu Hongquan via bank transfer. Wang Hui, through the Weida Company website advertising, falsely purported to be the anti-tumor drug sales center of Hengyu Company to sell anti-tumor drugs to the public. The defendant Zhang Xiaofeng, knowing that Weida Company did not have the qualifications to sell drugs and that he was not an employee of Hengyu Company, still assisted Wang Hui in picking up and arranging the delivery of the drugs. The imported brand anti-tumor drugs seized from the Weida Company warehouse were all determined to be counterfeit drugs upon inspection.

(II) Judgment

The Xi'an Intermediate People's Court, in its judgment, and the Shaanxi High People's Court, in its ruling, held that the defendants Wang Hui, Xu Hongde, Yu Hongquan, and Zhang Xiaofeng, in order to seek illegal gains, violated the national drug quality management system, disregarded the lives and health of patients, and produced and sold counterfeit imported anti-tumor drugs. Among them, defendant Wang Hui sold counterfeit drugs in the amount of RMB 2.388 million, and defendant Zhang Xiaofeng assisted Wang Hui in selling counterfeit drugs. Their conduct constituted the crime of selling counterfeit drugs. Defendants Xu Hongde and Yu Hongquan engaged in the production and sale of counterfeit drugs, with Xu Hongde's sale amount reaching RMB 1.9076 million and Yu Hongquan's sale amount reaching over RMB 480,000. Their conduct constituted the crime of producing and selling counterfeit drugs. The drugs sold by each defendant were all anti-tumor drugs, primarily used by cancer patients, and most were injectable drugs and prescription drugs, sufficient to seriously endanger human health, and the circumstances of the crime were egregious. The conduct of defendants Wang Hui and Zhang Xiaofeng also constituted the crime of selling counterfeit and substandard products. The conduct of defendants Xu Hongde and Yu Hongquan also constituted the crime of producing and selling counterfeit and substandard products. In accordance with the law, they were to be convicted and punished under the charge that provided for the heavier punishment. Zhang Xiaofeng was an accessory and was given a mitigated punishment in accordance with the law. The court ruled in accordance with the law: Defendant Wang Hui was convicted of the crime of selling counterfeit and substandard products and sentenced to 15 years of fixed-term imprisonment, and fined RMB 3 million. Defendant Xu Hongde was convicted of the crime of producing and selling counterfeit and substandard products and sentenced to 11 years and 8 months of fixed-term imprisonment, and fined RMB 2 million. Defendant Yu Hongquan was convicted of the crime of producing and selling counterfeit and substandard products and sentenced to 6 years of fixed-term imprisonment, and fined RMB 500,000. Defendant Zhang Xiaofeng was convicted of the crime of selling counterfeit and substandard products and sentenced to 1 year and 6 months of fixed-term imprisonment, and fined RMB 150,000. The illegal gains of each defendant were to be recovered and turned over to the state treasury. The seized drugs were to be confiscated and destroyed in accordance with the law.

The ruling for each defendant in this case became legally effective on July 12, 2011.

Case 9

Hu Xinhua, Zhou Rui, Li Chunlei, et al. — production and sale of counterfeit and substandard products, production and sale of fake drugs

(I) Basic Facts

Defendant Zhou Rui, male, born January 7, 1983, Han ethnicity, farmer.

Defendant Hu Xinhua, male, born March 3, 1966, Han ethnicity, farmer.

Defendant Li Chunlei, male, born February 10, 1982, Han ethnicity, farmer.

Defendant Ji Xu, male, born August 10, 1993, Han ethnicity, unemployed.

Defendant Liu Peng, male, born June 2, 1978, Han ethnicity, unemployed.

Defendant Wang Qingfang, male, born November 27, 1968, Han ethnicity, farmer.

Defendant Luo Cuihua, female, born February 25, 1970, Han ethnicity, farmer.

Defendant Xie Zhiguo, male, born April 10, 1978, Han ethnicity, farmer.

Defendant Ni Yun, male, born December 9, 1974, Han ethnicity, farmer.

Defendant Xiao Sanchun, male, born August 5, 1967, Han ethnicity, farmer.

From October 2008 to November 2010, the defendant Hu Xinhua illegally produced drugs such as "Jinghua Jiexuan Ning" and "Huoyi Tangping Capsules" for the treatment of psoriasis and diabetes in Tongzhou District, Beijing, and sold them for profit, with a total sales amount of over RMB 669,000. Hu Xinhua also instructed Hu Junhua (separately handled) to produce and sell drugs such as "Jinghua Jiexuan Ning" and "Huaxuan Kang", with a sales amount of over RMB 87,000. In addition, Hu Junhua, together with the defendant Xiao Sanchun, jointly produced the aforementioned drugs.

From February 2008 to November 2010, the defendant Zhou Rui, in order to seek illegal gains, purchased and sold in large quantities drugs such as "Jinghua Jiexuan Ning" and "Huaxuan Kang" sold by Hu Junhua and others, knowing they were counterfeit drugs, with a total sales amount of over RMB 1.885 million.

In January 2010, Zhou Rui and Hu Xinhua established a partnership in the name of Zhou Xuefeng (separately handled) to form Beijing Shengjinshuntong Commerce and Trade Co., Ltd., which specialized in providing services such as picking up goods, arranging mail delivery, and collecting payments on behalf of others for the production and sale of counterfeit drugs. By November 2010, the amount of counterfeit drugs sold reached over RMB 5.855 million. The defendants Li Chunlei, Ji Xu, and Liu Peng, as employees of the company, knowing that Beijing Shengjinshuntong Commerce and Trade Co., Ltd. was selling counterfeit drugs, specifically carried out assisting acts. The defendants Wang Qingfang and Luo Cuihua produced and through Beijing Shengjinshuntong Commerce and Trade Co., Ltd. sold drugs such as "Bencao Jiangtang Capsules", with a total sales amount of over RMB 322,000. The defendants Xie Zhiguo and Ni Yun illegally produced and through Beijing Shengjinshuntong Commerce and Trade Co., Ltd. sold drugs such as "Baicao Jiangya Capsules" and "Qufeng Huogu Wang".

Upon appraisal, various drugs seized from the warehouse of Beijing Shengjinshuntong Commerce and Trade Co., Ltd., and from Hu Xinhua, Zhou Rui, Wang Qingfang, Luo Cuihua, Xie Zhiguo, Ni Yun, Xiao Sanchun, Liu Peng, Ji Xu, Li Chunlei, and others, were all to be treated as counterfeit drugs.

(II) Judgment

The Tongzhou District People's Court of Beijing held in its judgment that the defendants Hu Xinhua, Wang Qingfang, Luo Cuihua, Xie Zhiguo, and Ni Yun produced and sold counterfeit drugs. Among them, Hu Xinhua's sales amount reached RMB 6.611 million, and Wang Qingfang and Luo Cuihua's sales amount reached over RMB 322,000. Their conduct simultaneously constituted both the crime of producing and selling counterfeit drugs and the crime of producing and selling counterfeit and substandard products. In accordance with the law, they were to be convicted and punished under the charge that provided for the heavier punishment. The defendants Zhou Rui, Li Chunlei, Liu Peng, and Ji Xu, knowing the drugs were counterfeit, sold them. Among them, Zhou Rui's sales amount reached over RMB 7.74 million, and Li Chunlei, Liu Peng, and Ji Xu's sales amount reached over RMB 5.855 million. Their conduct simultaneously constituted both the crime of selling counterfeit drugs and the crime of selling counterfeit and substandard products. In accordance with the law, they were to be convicted and punished under the charge that provided for the heavier punishment. The defendant Xiao Sanchun produced counterfeit drugs, which was sufficient to seriously endanger human health, and his conduct constituted the crime of producing counterfeit drugs. The defendants Hu Xinhua, Zhou Rui, Li Chunlei, Ji Xu, and Liu Peng constituted a joint crime. Among them, Hu Xinhua and Zhou Rui were principals, while Li Chunlei, Ji Xu, and Liu Peng were accessories, and they were to be given a mitigated punishment in accordance with the law. Ji Xu was under 18 years of age at the time of the crime and was to be given a mitigated punishment in accordance with the law. Based on the facts of the crime, circumstances, and degree of social harm of each defendant, the court ruled in accordance with the law: Defendant Hu Xinhua was convicted of the crime of producing and selling counterfeit and substandard products and sentenced to 15 years of fixed-term imprisonment, and fined RMB 4 million. Defendant Zhou Rui was convicted of the crime of selling counterfeit and substandard products and sentenced to 15 years of fixed-term imprisonment, and fined RMB 4 million. Defendant Li Chunlei was convicted of the crime of selling counterfeit and substandard products and sentenced to 7 years of fixed-term imprisonment, and fined RMB 1.5 million. Defendant Liu Peng was convicted of the crime of selling counterfeit and substandard products and sentenced to 7 years of fixed-term imprisonment, and fined RMB 1.5 million. Defendant Ji Xu was convicted of the crime of selling counterfeit and substandard products and sentenced to 5 years of fixed-term imprisonment, and fined RMB 1 million. Defendant Wang Qingfang was convicted of the crime of producing and selling counterfeit and substandard products and sentenced to 3 years and 6 months of fixed-term imprisonment, and fined RMB 200,000. Defendant Luo Cuihua was convicted of the crime of producing and selling counterfeit and substandard products and sentenced to 3 years of fixed-term imprisonment, and fined RMB 180,000. Defendant Xie Zhiguo was convicted of the crime of producing and selling counterfeit drugs and sentenced to 2 years and 6 months of fixed-term imprisonment, and fined RMB 80,000. Defendant Ni Yun was convicted of the crime of producing and selling counterfeit drugs and sentenced to 2 years of fixed-term imprisonment, and fined RMB 50,000. Defendant Xiao Sanchun was convicted of the crime of producing counterfeit drugs and sentenced to 1 year and 6 months of fixed-term imprisonment, and fined RMB 40,000. The seized tools, illicit money, and illicit goods were ordered to be confiscated. After the judgment was pronounced, none of the defendants appealed, and the prosecutorial authority did not protest. This judgment became legally effective on March 26, 2012.

Case 10

Wei Kaiyuan, Zhang Dazhi, He Zirui, et al. — sale of fake drugs

(I) Basic Facts

Defendant Zhang Dazhi, male, born January 7, 1967, Han ethnicity, self-employed.

Defendant He Zirui, male, born July 25, 1978, Han ethnicity, worker.

Defendant Chen Xianrou, female, born February 5, 1974, Zhuang ethnicity, self-employed.

Defendant Wei Kaiyuan, male, born November 29, 1971, Zhuang ethnicity, Deputy General Manager of Laibin Xin'er Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.

Defendant Yu Zongqu, male, born November 25, 1964, Han ethnicity, practicing physician.

Defendant Meng Meng, male, born September 9, 1982, Zhuang ethnicity, salesman of Laibin Jiushanhong Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.

Defendant Huang Guang'en, male, born November 18, 1983, Zhuang ethnicity, salesman of Laibin Xin'er Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.

From July to November 2009, the defendant Wei Kaiyuan, in the name of Guangzhou Husheng Biological Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd., sold counterfeit "human rabies vaccines" from multiple batches, including batch number 20090726, which he had purchased from others, to the Beiwu Township Health Center, Honghe Health Center Xiazhi Branch, Zhenglong Township Health Center, Gao'an Township Health Center, and Wushan Township Health Center in Laibin City, Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, totaling over one hundred doses. On the afternoon of October 21, 2009, the victim Ye Jianhua (deceased, age 6) was bitten by a dog. His father, Ye Xian'gan, washed the wound with soap and water and immediately took him to Zhenglong Township Health Center in Xingbin District, Laibin City, for treatment. From that day until December 3, 2009, the health center administered to Ye Jianhua, following standard procedures, the counterfeit "human rabies vaccine" with batch number 20090726 that Wei Kaiyuan had sold to the health center. Subsequently, Ye Jianhua showed abnormal reactions and was sent to the Fourth People's Hospital of Nanning on December 9, 2009, where he died despite rescue efforts. The hospital diagnosed the cause of death as rabies. Investigation revealed that from August to December 2009, the defendant Yang Bin (who fled while on bail pending trial, case suspended) purchased counterfeit "human rabies vaccines" from Chen Bin (separately handled) and sold them at a markup to the defendant Zhang Dazhi. Zhang Dazhi sold them at a markup to the defendant He Zirui, who sold them at a markup to the defendants Chen Xianrou, Yu Zongqu, Meng Meng, and others. Chen Xianrou sold the counterfeit "human rabies vaccines" at a markup to Wei Kaiyuan, Yu Zongqu sold them at a markup to others, Meng Meng sold them at a markup to the defendant Huang Guang'en, and Huang Guang'en sold them at a markup to others.

During the first instance, the defendants Yang Bin, Zhang Dazhi, He Zirui, Chen Xianrou, and Wei Kaiyuan compensated the victim's family with RMB 200,000.

(II) Judgment

The Laibin Intermediate People's Court and the Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region High People's Court held in their judgments that the defendants Zhang Dazhi, He Zirui, Chen Xianrou, Wei Kaiyuan, Yu Zongqu, Meng Meng, and Huang Guang'en, by selling counterfeit "human rabies vaccines," which were sufficient to seriously endanger human health, had committed the crime of selling counterfeit drugs. The victim Ye Jianhua died of rabies, and there was a causal relationship between his death and the use of the counterfeit "human rabies vaccine" with batch number 20090726 that Wei Kaiyuan had sold to Zhenglong Township Health Center. Although Wei Kaiyuan had purchased counterfeit "human rabies vaccines" from Chen Xianrou, he had also purchased them from others, so the evidence was insufficient to establish that the counterfeit "human rabies vaccine" with batch number 20090726 sold by Wei Kaiyuan to Zhenglong Township Health Center indeed originated from the defendants Zhang Dazhi, He Zirui, and Chen Xianrou. Zhang Dazhi, He Zirui, Chen Xianrou, and Wei Kaiyuan voluntarily compensated the victim's family, showing a certain degree of remorse, and could be given a lighter punishment at the court's discretion. The court, in accordance with the law, sentenced each defendant for the crime of selling counterfeit drugs, imposing the following sentences: Defendant Wei Kaiyuan was sentenced to 15 years of fixed-term imprisonment and fined RMB 50,000; Defendant Zhang Dazhi was sentenced to 3 years of fixed-term imprisonment and fined RMB 30,000; Defendant He Zirui was sentenced to 3 years of fixed-term imprisonment and fined RMB 30,000; Defendant Chen Xianrou was sentenced to 3 years of fixed-term imprisonment and fined RMB 8,800; Defendant Yu Zongqu was sentenced to 1 year and 6 months of fixed-term imprisonment and fined RMB 30,000; Defendant Meng Meng was sentenced to 1 year and 6 months of fixed-term imprisonment and fined RMB 30,000; and Defendant Huang Guang'en was sentenced to 1 year and 6 months of fixed-term imprisonment and fined RMB 30,000. The illegal gains of each defendant were to be confiscated and turned over to the state treasury.

The judgments for each defendant in this case became legally effective on January 12, 2012.
